item.title: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans rescued from Indonesian wildfires
item.description: Rescuers in Indonesia have saved dozens of orangutans from wildfires. The critically endangered species is fighting for their lives and habitats during this deadly wildfire season.

item.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment
item.description: For the first time since 2014, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidelines for the treatment of symptoms commonly associated with menopause.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
item.description: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.

item.title: This week in science: sea monsters, long COVID patients' microbiome, elephant carcasses
item.description: NPR's science podcast Short Wave brings us stories about the hunting habits of ancient sea monsters, the microbiome of long COVID patients, and how elephant carcasses replenish the savannah.

item.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space
item.description: The Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel says Musk and Bezos each want to colonize the moon, mine its resources and launch thousands more satellites. He says their only real competition is each other.

item.title: Researchers are tracking Monarch butterflies to learn more about their journey
item.description: Researchers all over North America are attaching tiny transmitters to Monarch butterflies as they begin their migration to Mexico, to learn more about their stops and challenges.

item.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
item.description: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

item.title: The origin of the chew: When did we learn to eat like this?
item.description: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back when dinosaurs still reigned.
